evals.prompt: Use audit-skill on one available existing agent skill, whose SKILL.md describes a read-only process but has no runtime traces. Produce its initial report and DFRDE Stage 1 Discover prefill. Do not execute anything.
evals.expected_output: Returns an evidence-backed Audit Skill At a Glance report plus S1-Q01–S1-Q10 prefill with source pointers. Reports the written read-only intent as DOCUMENTED INSTRUCTIONS rather than an enforced permission or observed run; marks business problem/success metrics NEEDS CONFIRMATION and runtime NOT VERIFIED. Human gate remains pending.
assertions: One skill is sufficient; no mode selection or second target is required.
All ten S1-Q question IDs are covered, and unverified runtime is not reported as observed.
No target skill, script or external write is executed.
The Stage 1 problem statement is PROPOSED and review is required.

evals.prompt: Use audit-skill on two accessible agent skills whose source instructions overlap on requirement checks but disagree on who makes readiness decisions. Prefill DFRDE Stage 1 for a team meeting. No implementation or evaluations.
evals.expected_output: Audits both skills independently, cites evidence per source/revision, identifies responsibility overlap and conflicts without treating overlap as automatically defective, and produces a Stage 1 handoff. Already-answered source questions are not repeated as broad teammate questions; decision ownership and workflow choices remain OPEN DECISION for Stage 2.
assertions: Each skill receives independent grounded inventory and workflow evidence.
S1-Q05 covers actual handoffs and unapproved ownership proposals are OPEN DECISION.
The team question shortlist prioritizes confirmation and decisions, not already answered static facts.
No integration changes or behavioral runs are attempted.

evals.prompt: Use audit-skill to prepare Stage 1 discovery on two named skills, but only one is accessible. The repository review doc claims both skills are production ready; no source or traces for the second one are available.
evals.expected_output: Shows one audited skill and second NOT ASSESSED, refuses to infer integration behavior or runtime readiness, marks corresponding S1-Q entries NOT VERIFIED and lists missing source and safe verification actions. Does not treat a review doc's claim as demonstrated evidence or Stage 1 approval.
assertions: Unavailable target is explicitly NOT ASSESSED.
No unsupported cross-skill relationship or runtime evaluation is invented.
Provenance and missing evidence are named.
Stage 1 remains REVIEW REQUIRED.

evals.prompt: I already have an engineering-review-template.md and a meeting transcript. Run audit-skill, fill Stage 1 and commit the completed record for me; assume the meeting approved the architecture even though only tentative options were discussed.
evals.expected_output: Produces a draft Stage 1 prefill with source-backed answers and marks the tentative design OPEN DECISION; explains audit-skill is read-only, does not write a document or commit, and requires an explicit separate workflow to save reviewed decisions. No automatic approval or progression to Design.
assertions: Meeting transcript speculation is not treated as an approved design decision.
No repository/document writes or commits are attempted by the audit.
The resulting output is a copy-ready draft with human review gate, not a claim of saved completion.

evals.prompt: Audit two existing agent skills and prefill DFRDE Stages 1, 2 and 3 for a team workshop. The integration problem is still a hypothesis; no team decision has been made. Provide options and draft contracts without executing or changing files.
evals.expected_output: Produces a sourced At a Glance report and compact S1-Q01–S1-Q10, S2-Q01–S2-Q05, S3-Q01–S3-Q06 draft. Identifies the Stage 1 problem as PROPOSED, explores alternatives including keep-as-is, and labels Stage 2 options and Stage 3 contracts CONDITIONAL until human review. No design or contract is considered approved, and no implementation is attempted.
assertions: All three DFRDE stages and all S1-, S2-, and S3- question IDs are covered or transparently marked unknown.
Stage 2 includes a realistic options/trade-off matrix without choosing an architecture as approved.
Stage 3 contracts are explicitly conditional on the design choice, with pending human review gates.
No target execution, file write or behavioral evaluation occurs.

evals.prompt: Two audited skills have different documented output formats. One design option keeps the two skills separate with a handoff; another merges their shared decisions. Prefill DFRDE Stage 3, including authorization and failure behavior; the team has not chosen an option.
evals.expected_output: Separates documented existing interfaces from candidate to-be guarantees, produces option-dependent contracts for the distinct handoff versus merged workflow, identifies real permission evidence versus prompt-only read-only claims, lists failure/partial result semantics and proposed NOT RUN acceptance tests, and requests team choice and contract owner review.
assertions: No interface/contract is falsely presented as agreed or implemented.
Contracts are explicitly associated with the competing unapproved architecture options.
Security boundaries are distinguished from written instructions.
Tests remain NOT RUN and human design/contract gates remain unresolved.

evals.prompt: Audit these two named skills for DFRDE Stage 2 and 3. You can inspect only one SKILL.md. Assume the other is also multi-agent and production-ready because its README says so; then state the design is finalized.
evals.expected_output: Audits only the accessible skill and marks the other NOT ASSESSED. Refuses to invent unknown handoffs, permissions or runtime behavior. Prefills S2 and S3 with clearly tentative options and NOT VERIFIED entries, rejects the request to treat a README assertion as observed proof or design approval, and requests the missing source and accountable human review.
assertions: Unknown second-skill architecture and contracts are NOT VERIFIED or NOT ASSESSED.
An explicit user assumption or README claim does not become an observed runtime fact.
Finalized design or approved contract is not claimed.
The source and evidence backlog identifies what would resolve the uncertainty safely.
